text:
alex: incident-bot flagged a node flap in us-west-2, multiple containers OOMing on paged-attn allocator. slow resident growth over hours, looks like fragmentation + leak.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT: sev2 - suspected kv-cache / paged-attn memory creep. Runbook link: /runbooks/paged-kv-leak :rotating_light:
maria: jumping in. which hosts? any customer impact?
alex: hosts: rwinf-usw2-03 and rwinf-usw2-04. runtime-serve containers crash-looping. logs show CUDA errors then driver resets. metrics show rising page fragmentation and free-list depletion.
ryan: starting live mitigation. will flip aggressive eviction and reduce batching on those hosts.
deploy-bot: deploy started: oncall/evict-policy patch -> env update on rwinf-usw2-03
alex: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-17T22:10:12Z runtime ERROR: CUDA error (out of memory)
alloc_paged: slab split failure, free-list empty
kv_map: page_ref=0x3f12 corrupt?
mem: resident 18.2GB -> 19.5GB over 3h (leak)
OOM at 22:12:37, container restarted
```
jordan: can we failover traffic? prefer send to us-west-1 fallback pool to avoid customer impact.
ops-liz: routing now, shifting ~35% to fallback model in us-west-1. health checks show rwinf-usw2-03 failing, 04 flapping. customer-ops: heads up — degraded tail latency for some customers.
customer-ops: notified top-tier customers, no escalations yet. monitoring for error spikes.
maria: any quick config to stop the slow creep? maybe cap batch size or disable prefix/KV caching temporarily?
ryan: applied env overrides: KV_CACHE_MAX_PAGES=200, BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=512, PREFIX_CACHE=off on 03. restarting pods to clear warm KV.
alex: after restart 03 flattened memory usage. 04 still drifting and showing `kv_page_map corruption` in logs, collecting heap/core dump.
jordan: if full heap dump is heavy, prefer core + sampling. need allocation traces. @maria can you grab nvprof and allocation histograms?
maria: grabbing nvprof + kv-usage hist. initial correlation: long-context sessions (>>8k tokens) increase paged allocations steadily.
oncall-bot: :pushpin: Runbook step executed: aggressive-evict toggle ON (initiated by ryan). Monitoring 10m window.
alex: after 8m memory on 03 flatlined. 04 still drifting; eviction toggle didn't apply because agent was on v2.12.
ryan: rolling agent to v2.16 now on 04 to pick up eviction toggle codepath. will do staggered restart.
deploy-bot: agent rollout started: rwinf-usw2-04 -> v2.16 (staggered)
ops-liz: agent roll ETA ~12m. moving background batch jobs off these machines.
alex: once agent rolled, eviction engaged and mem growth stopped on 04. node remains in failed health but not OOMing. traffic remains routed to fallback until stable.
jordan: action items: 1) full postmortem if leak confirmed 2) autopatch/agent upgrade guard so eviction toggles don't fail 3) add eviction-by-age alert and fragmentation ratio alert 4) follow up with model team on long-context session behavior.
maria: i'll own 1 and 4. will pull evals to reproduce slow leak with long-context stress.
ryan: i'll own 2 and 3, open tickets and add canary job for paged-attn stress.
alex: tl;dr: slow paged-attn allocator leak -> allocator fragmentation -> node flaps -> CUDA OOM -> container crashes. Live mitigations: aggressive eviction, batch cap, disable prefix cache, agent rollout, traffic routing to fallback. No customer escalations so far. will monitor 30m.
customer-ops: we'll push updates to customers every 30m. thanks for the quick response :heart:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied, monitoring. temporary page cleared. reopen if recurrence or new OOMs observed.
